712201.lxx: in LXX chiefly for כָּסָה pi.
712201.full: συν-καλύπτω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX chiefly for כָּסָה pi. ;] to veil or cover completely: with accusative, pass., Luk.12:2.† (AS)

712202.full: συν-κάμπτω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Psa.68:10, 23 (מעד hi.), etc. ;] to bend completely, bend together: τ. νῶτον, figuratively, Rom.11:10 (LXX).† (AS)

712203.lxx: in LXX: Psa.49:17 (יָרַד), Wis.10:13, Dan LXX TH 3:49 *
712203.full: συν-κατα-βαίνω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Psa.49:17 (יָרַד), Wis.10:13, Dan LXX TH 3:49 * ;] to go down with: Act.25:5. In late writers also metaphorically (Wis, l.with), to condescend, on WH. see Rutherford, NPhr., 485 f.† (AS)

712206.full: to mix in with, mingle, blend with , Χάριτας Μούσαις συγκαταμιγνύς (Euripides):—;Pass. to be absorbed in a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

712210.full: 1. Pass. to lie together , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. as Pass. of συντίθημι, to be composed or compounded , ἔκ τινων of certain parts, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 3. of written works, to be composed , (Thucydides), etc. 4. to be contrived, concocted , (Euripides), etc. 5. to be agreed on by two parties, (Thucydides): in participle agreed on, arranged , αἱ συγκείμεναι ἡμέραι (Herdotus Historicus); κατὰ τὰ συγκείμενα according to the terms agreed on , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐκ τῶν ξυγκειμένων (Thucydides) 6. impersonal σύγκειται, it has been or is agreed on , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; so, συγκειμένου σφι, with infinitive, since they had agreed to . . , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

712211.full: to pierce together, to stab at once , Lat. telis confodere, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., ἔμελλε συγκεντηθήσεσθαι (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: to mix or blend together, compound
712212.full: συν-κεράννυμι (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Dan LXX 2:43 (עֲרַב ithpa.), 2Ma.15:39 * ;] to mix or blend together, compound: with accusative, 1Co.12:24; ptcp. pf. pass., Heb.4:2, T, WH, mg., R, mg.; id., of persons, with dative instr., to be united with, agree with, ib., WH, txt., R, txt. (see Westc., in l).† (AS)

s: as with a thunderbolt, shiver in pieces
712214.full: to strike with or as with a thunderbolt, shiver in pieces , (Euripides) (ML)

s: to shut together, enclose, shut in on all sides
712223.full: συν-κλείω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX chiefly for סגר ;] to shut together, enclose, shut in on all sides: of a catch of fish, Luk.5:6; metaphorically (Psa.31:9, al.), Rom.11:32, Gal.3:22-23.† (AS)

712225.full: 1. called together, summoned , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. ς. ἐκκλησία at Athens, an assembly specially summoned by the στρατηγός (opposite to the ordinary meetings, αἱ κυρίαι); Decret. quoted in (Demosthenes Orator):—;generally, σύγκλητος (i.e. ἐκκλησία); a legislative body , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

s: to take up a body for burial
712229.full: συν-κομίζω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Job.5:26 (עָלָה) * ;] __1. to bring together, collect (Hdt., Xen., al.). __2. to take up a body for burial (Soph., Aj., 1048): Act.8:2 (see Field, Notes, 116).† (AS)

712230.full: 1. to break up, cut up , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to thrash soundly, pound well , (Xenophon Historicus);—;Pass., perfect infinitive συγκεκόφθαι (Aristophanes Comicus); participle συγκεκομμένος (Euripides) (ML)

712231.full: a mixing together, commixture, blending, tempering , (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

712233.full: συν-κρίνω (Rec. συγκ-) [in LXX chiefly for פָּתַר ;] __1. to compound, combine: 1Co.2:13, R, mg.1 (Lft., Notes, 180 f.). __2. In Arist. and later writers (Wis.7:29, a1.) = παραβάλλω, to compare: 1Co, l.with, R, txt. (Field, Notes, 168), 2Co.10:12 __3. In LXX, of dreams, to interpret (Gen.40:8, 1Co, l.with, R, mg. 2 (but see reff. supr.).† (AS)

712234.full: 1. a compounding , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. a comparing, comparison , (Aristotle Philosopher), etc. (ML)

712235.full: 1. to strike together; ς. τὼ χεῖρε to clap the hands for joy, (Xenophon Historicus); but also to smite them together in grief, (Lucian):—;Pass. to be applauded , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to hammer or weld together , (Aristophanes Comicus): hence, to weld a number of men into one body, i. e. organise them, (Demosthenes Orator), etc.:—;perfect passive participle συγκεκροτημένος well-trained, in good discipline , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

712239.full: 1. to join with another in founding or colonising , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. Pass., perfect participle συνεκτισμένος well-cultivated. (ML)

712240.full: συν-κύπτω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Job.9:27 (עָזַב), Sir.12:11 19:26 * ;] __1. to bend forwards (Arist., al.). __2. to be bowed down: Luk.13:11.† (AS)

712242.full: συν-χαίρω (Rec. συγ-), [in LXX: Gen.21:6 (צָחַק), 3Ma.1:8 R * ;] __1. to rejoice with: with dative of person(s), Luk.1:58 15:6, 9, Php.2:17-18, EV; with dative of thing(s), 1Co.12:26 13:6. __2. to congratulate (Æschin., Polyb., al.): Phi, l.with (Lft., in I.; cf. MM, xxiv).† (AS)

s: confound, throw into confusion, stir up trouble
712243.lxx: in LXX for בָּלַל, רָגַז, etc.
712243.full: συν-χέω (Rec. συγ-), [in LXX for בָּלַל, רָגַז, etc. ;] to pour together, commingle, confuse; metaphorically, confound, throw into confusion, stir up trouble: Act.21:27 (cf. συν-χύννω).† (AS)

712245.full: σύγχυσις, -εως, ἡ (συγχέω), [in LXX: Gen.11:9 (בָּבֶל), 1Ki.5:6 5:12(11) 1Ki.14:20 (מְהוּמָה) * ;] confusion: of a popular uproar, Act.19:29.† (AS)

712248.full: συν-ζεύγνυμι (Rec. συζ-), [in LXX: Eze.1:11, 23 (חָבַר) * ;] to yoke to­gether: metaphorically, of union in wedlock, Mat.19:6, Mrk.10:9.† (AS)

712252.full: the fruit of the συκάμινος, a mulberry , Lat. morum, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

712253.full: συκάμινος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX for שִׁקְמָה (pl.) ;] the mulberry tree (Lat. morus; cf. μόρον, 1Ma.6:34 *), the sycamine: Luk.17:6. (In LXX, σ. appears to represent the συκόμορος (see: συκομορέα), but St. Luke distinguishes between the two; see ICC, in l; DB, iv, 634.) † (AS)

712254.full: συκῆ (contr. fr. συκέα), -ῆς, ἡ (σῦκον), [in LXX for תְּאֵן ;] a fig-tree: Mat.21:19-21 24:32, Mrk.11:13, 20-21 13:28, Luk.13:6-7 21:29, Jhn.1:49, 51, Jas.3:12, Rev.6:13.† (AS)

712255.full: σῦκον, -ου, τό [in LXX for תְּאֵן ] a fig: Mat.7:16, Mrk.11:13, Luk.6:44 Jas.3:12.† (AS)

712256.full: συκοφαντέω, -ῶ (σῦκον, φαίνω), [in LXX: Gen.43:18 (גָּלַל hithpo.), Lev.19:11 (שָׁקַר pi.), Job.35:9, Psa.119:122, Pro.14:31 2:16 28:3, Ecc.4:1 (עָשַׁק) ;] to act the συκοφάντης (on conjectures as to the origin of the term, see LS, see word), to accuse falsely (Aristoph., Xen., al.): Luk.3:14 (R, mg.) Luk.19:8 (RV, exact wrongfully; but cf. Hatch, Essays, 89 ff., see also Field, Notes, 56 f.; MM, xxiv).† (AS)

s: one who informed against persons exporting figs
one who brings figs to light by shaking the tree
one who makes rich men yield up their fruit by false accusations)
712257.full: a false accuser, slanderer , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; (never used in the modern sense of sycophant , i. e. κόλαξ); generally, a false adviser , (Demosthenes Orator) (Commonly derived from σῦκον, φαίνω, one who informed against persons exporting figs from Attica: better perhaps a fig-shewer , i. e. one who brings figs to light by shaking the tree (the figs having been hidden in the thick foliage); and then, metaphorically, one who makes rich men yield up their fruit by false accusations). (ML)

712258.full: 1. false accusation, slander, calumny , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 2. a sophism , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

712260.full: συλάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ep. Jer.1:18 * ;] with accusative of person(s), to strip, plunder, spoil: 2Co.11:8.† (AS)

712262.lxx: in LXX for תָּפַשׂ, הָרָה, etc.
712262.full: συλ-λαμβάνω [in LXX for תָּפַשׂ, הָרָה, etc. ;] __1. with accusative, to bring together, collect. __2. to seize, take: with accusative of person(s), as a prisoner, Mat.26:55, Mrk.14:48, Luk.22:54, Jhn.18:12, Act.1:16 12:3; pass., Act.23:27; mid., in sense of act., Act.26:21; σ. ἄγραν ἰχθύων, Luk.5:9. __3. C. dative of person(s), to take part with, assist, succour; mid., in same sense: Luk.5:7, Php.4:3. __4. Of a woman, to conceive: absol., Luk.1:24; before ἐν γαστρί, Luk.1:31; with accusative, Luk.1:36; ib. before ἐν τ. κοιλίᾳ, Luk.2:21; metaphorically, of lust producing sin, Jas.1:15.† (AS)

s: to bring together, collect, gather up
712263.full: συλ-λέγω [in LXX chiefly for לָקַט ;] to bring together, collect, gather up: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.13:28-30; pass., Mat.13:40; with accusative, before ἀπό, Mat.7:16; id. before ἐκ, Mat.13:41, Luk.6:44; before εἰς, Mat.13:48.† (AS)

712265.full: 1. a taking together: a seizing, arresting , ποιεῖσθαι ξύλληψιν to arrest , (Thucydides) 2. conception , (Plutarch) (ML)

712266.full: 1. a gathering, collecting , (Thucydides): metaphorically, ἐν γενείου ξυλλογῇ τριχώματος in the first harvest of a beard, i. e. in early manhood, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. a levying of soldiers, Lat. conscriptio, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. a summary, recapitulation , (Demosthenes Orator) 4. (from Pass.) an assembly, meeting , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

712267.lxx: in LXX chiefly for חָשַׁב pi.
712267.full: συλ-λογίζομαι [in LXX chiefly for חָשַׁב pi. ;] __1. to compute. __2. to reason: Luk.20:5.† (AS)

712268.full: 1. computation , (Plato Philosophus) 2. a conclusion, inference from premisses , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

s: to be moved to grief by sympathy
712272.full: συν-λυπέω (Rec. συλλ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: Psa.69:20, Isa.51:19 (נוּד) * ;] to make to grieve with (Arist.). Pass., to be moved to grief by sympathy: before ἐπί, with dative, Mrk.3:5.† (AS)

712273.g: to rest under the same roof.
s: to help to solve a difficulty
to rest under the same roof
712273.full: 1. to help in loosing , (Euripides):—; to help to solve a difficulty or end a quarrel , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to rest under the same roof , (Aeschulus Tragicus); compare καταλύω. (ML)

s: Of events, to come to pass, happen
712277.lxx: in LXX for עָשָׂה, קָרָא, קָרָה, etc.
712277.full: συμ-βαίνω [in LXX for עָשָׂה, קָרָא, קָרָה, etc. ;] __1. to stand with the feet together. __2. to come together, come to terms. __3. Of events, to come to pass, happen: with dative of person(s), Mrk.10:32, Act.3:10 20:19, 1Co.10:11, 1Pe.4:12, 2Pe.2:22; absol., τὰ σνμβεβηκότα, Luk.24:14 (cf. 1Ma.4:26); with accusative and nf., Act.21:35.† (AS)

s: to meet with, fall in with
712278.lxx: in LXX: 2Ch.25:19 (גָּרָה hith.), Isa.46:6 (זוּל), Jer.43:3 (סוּת hi.), Wis.5:8, al.
712278.full: συν-βάλλω (Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: 2Ch.25:19 (גָּרָה hith.), Isa.46:6 (זוּל), Jer.43:3 (סוּת hi.), Wis.5:8, al. ;] to throw together, hence, __(a) of speech (before λόγους, Eur., al.), to discuss, confer (sc. λόγους): with dative of person(s), Luk.11:53, WH, mg., Act.17:18; before πρὸς ἀλλήλους, Act.4:15; __(b) to reflect, consider, ponder: ἐν τ. καρδίᾳ, Luk.2:19; __(with) to meet with, fall in with: Act.20:14; in hostile sense, εἰς πόλεμον, with dative (εἰς μάχην, Polyb.), Luk.14:31; __(d) mid., to contribute (Polyb., al.; cf. MM, xxiv): Act.18:27.† (AS)

s: to join or knit together, unite
712280.lxx: in LXX: Exo.4:12, 15, Lev.10:11, Jdg.13:8, Psa.32:8 (יָרָה hi.); Exo.18:16, Deu.4:9, Isa.40:13 (יָדַע hi.), Isa.40:14 (בִּין hi.), Da TH Dan.9:22 (שָׂכַל hi.) *
712280.full: συν-βιβάζω (Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: Exo.4:12, 15, Lev.10:11, Jdg.13:8, Psa.32:8 (יָרָה hi.); Exo.18:16, Deu.4:9, Isa.40:13 (יָדַע hi.), Isa.40:14 (בִּין hi.), Da TH Dan.9:22 (שָׂכַל hi.) * ;] __1. to join or knit together, unite: Eph.4:16, Col.2:2 (but see infr.), Col.2:19. __2. to compare, consider, conclude (Plat.): Act.16:10. __3. to deduce, prove, demonstrate (Arist.): Act.9:22. __4. As in LXX ("translation Greek," = ἐμβιβάζω, metaphorically), to teach, instruct: 1Co.2:16 Act.19:33, R, mg. (also in Vg., Col.2:2, instructi, but see supr.).† (AS)

712287.full: 1. a coming together, meeting, joining , (Xenophon Historicus): the juncture of two parts, the end , Lat. commissura, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. in hostile sense, an encounter, engagement, battle , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. = συμβόλαιον II, a contract, covenant , (Aristotle Philosopher); in (Aristophanes Comicus) Ach. there is a play on signfs. II and III, encounter and accounts, charge and charges. 4. in plural, συμβολαί were contributions for a common meal, πίνειν ἀπὸ συμβολῶν, like de symbolis(Terentius Grammaticus Latinus) entertainment itself, a picnic , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

712289.full: 1. a sign or token by which one infers a thing, [variant datesTragica Adespota; λαμπάδος τὸ σύμβολον the token of the beacon-fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;often in plural, of marks on the body, (Euripides); of omens , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. a pledge or pawn , on which money was advanced, (Lysias Orator) 3. in plural tallies , Lat. tesserae hospitales, i.e. the halves of a bone or coin, which two persons broke between them, each keeping one piece, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 4. at Athens, a ticket, counter , Lat. tessera, such as were given to the dicasts, on presenting which they received their fee, (Demosthenes Orator) 5. a permit or licence to reside, given to aliens , (Aristophanes Comicus); a ticket given by each person who joined in a picnic, to be presented for payment at the end (compare συμβολή IV), (Aristophanes Comicus) 6. in Eccl. the distinctive mark of Christians, a confession of faith, a creed , Lat. symbolum. 7. in legal phrase, σύμβολα were covenants between two states for protection of commerce , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; σύμβολα ποιεῖσθαι πρὸς πόλιν to make a commercial treaty with a state, τὰ ς. συγχέειν to violate such treaty , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

712292.full: 1. to advise, counsel , Lat. consulere alicui, with dative pers. et infinitive, to advise one to do a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. without the infinitive, ς. τινί τι (Herdotus Historicus); ς. τι to recommend a measure, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass., τὰ συμβουλευόμενα the advice given , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. absolute to advise, give advice , (Sophocles Tragicus); ὁ συμβουλεύων or -εύσας, an adviser , Lat. auctor sententiae, (Aristotle Philosopher) 4. Mid. to consult with a person, i. e. ask his advice , Lat. consulere aliquem, with dative, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: absolute to consult, deliberate , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

712294.full: συμβούλιον, -ου, τό (σύμβουλος), [in LXX: 4Ma.17:17 א * ;] a word of the Græco-Roman period (of. Lat. consilium, and see Deiss., BS, 238) = cl. συμβουλία (Arist., Xen.), __1. counsel: σ. λαμβάνειν, Mat.12:14 22:15 27:7 28:12; διδόναι, Mrk.3:6 (ποιεῖν, Rec.); ποιεῖν, Mrk.15:1 (ἑτοιμάζειν, WH, mg.). __2. By meton., a council (4Mac, l.with א; συνέδριον, AR): Act.25:12 (see MM, xxiv).† (AS)

712295.lxx: in LXX for יָעַץ and cogn. forms
712295.full: σύμβουλος, -ου, ὁ (σύν, βουλή), [in LXX for יָעַץ and cogn. forms ;] a counsellor, adviser: Rom.11:34 (LXX).† (AS)

s: An aged worshipper in the Temple
712297.full: Συμεών, ὁ indecl., (Heb. שִׁמְעוֹן), Simeon (so always AV; RV in Luk.2:25, 34 only), Symeon, a Heb. name for which the Gk. Σίμων, which see, was also used; __1. the son of Jacob (Gen.29:33): Rev.7:7. __2. An ancestor of our Lord: Luk.3:30 __3. An aged worshipper in the Temple: Luk.2:25, 34. __4. One surnamed Niger: Act.13:1. __5. The apostle Peter: Act.15:14, 2Pe.1:1 (R, txt., WH, txt., Σίμων).† (AS)

712298.full: to be an ally, to be in alliance , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;generally, to help, aid, succour , τινί (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be assisted , (Lucian) (ML)

712299.full: 1. an alliance offensive and defensive (opposite to an ἐπιμαχία, defensive) , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: συμμαχίαν ποιεῖσθαι πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus); τινί (Thucydides) 2. generally, the duty of an ally , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. = τὸ συμμαχικόν, the body of allies , (Herdotus Historicus): also, the country of one's allies , (Thucydides) 4. an allied or auxiliary force , (Thucydides) (ML)
